penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Server-side GTM migration involves reviewing each client's existing tag configuration, testing tracking accuracy post-migration, and debugging broken tags — work that requires per-client human technical judgment and cannot be fully automated by Claude.

rationale: The buyer — technical founders and developers at real businesses with SEO stakes — is plausible and agencies already charge $500–$3k for this work, confirming willingness to pay. However, each server-side GTM migration requires hands-on review of a client's unique tag setup, post-migration QA, and debugging, making per-customer human fulfillment unavoidable and dropping operational_autonomy to 5 (below the 7 floor). The penalty for human fulfillment further reduces the total to 3.8. A fully informational product (guide/checklist) would score higher on autonomy but likely not command meaningful prices against free alternatives.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable as an autonomous micro-service because every real migration engagement requires reviewing a client's specific GTM container, testing tracking accuracy, and debugging — Claude cannot reliably perform this per-client technical audit without human QA. A pure content/guide product (e.g. a $29 PDF checklist) is buildable autonomously but unlikely to generate meaningful recurring revenue against the volume of free tutorials already available. Drop in favor of higher-autonomy opportunities.
notes: Failing build_gate: operational_autonomy (5, floor 7). Penalty: requires_human_fulfillment (-1.5) because actual migration delivery requires per-client human technical work. The informational-only variant avoids the penalty but faces a free-content ceiling.
